uncited: - **Inputs**: $t_{max}$, the maximum rendering time among all processors; $t_{avg}$, the average rendering time across all processors.
No specific data structures are required for the calculation itself.
The inputs are scalar values derived from timing logs of the parallel rendering execution.
- $t_{avg} = \frac{1}{P} \sum_{i=1}^{P} t_i$ is the mean rendering time across $P$ processors.
- $t_{max} = \max_{i=1}^{P} t_i$ is the maximum rendering time observed among the $P$ processors.
Measure the total rendering time $t_i$ for each processor $i$ from $1$ to $P$.
Compute the average time $t_{avg}$ by summing all $t_i$ and dividing by $P$.
Identify the maximum time $t_{max}$ from the set of all $t_i$.
- **Distribution Blindness**: The formulation does not reveal the actual distribution of the imbalanced load.
For example, two scenarios with the same $l$ may have vastly different variance profiles among the intermediate processors.

- **Sensitivity to Outliers**: Since $t_{max}$ is in the denominator, a single straggler processor significantly increases the metric, potentially masking the efficiency of the majority of processors.
- **Strengths**: Simple to compute from standard timing logs; provides a single scalar for comparing different load balancing strategies or decomposition schemes.
- **Limitations**: Does not indicate which processors are imbalanced or the nature of the imbalance (e.g., geometric vs. data-driven).
